questions.q: What delivery guarantee does Salesforce actually make for platform events and CDC events?
options: Exactly-once delivery — a subscriber will never see a duplicate
At-least-once delivery — the event is guaranteed to arrive, but possibly more than once
At-most-once delivery — the event might never arrive, but will never duplicate
No delivery guarantee of any kind is made
questions.explain: Salesforce guarantees at-least-once delivery: events will arrive, but retries and reconnects can cause the same event to be delivered more than once, so subscribers must tolerate duplicates.

questions.q: How long are platform events and CDC events retained for replay?
options: 24 hours
7 days
72 hours
30 days
questions.explain: Platform events and CDC events are retained for 72 hours; a subscriber offline longer than that can no longer recover the missed events by replay.

questions.q: What should a subscriber use a stored Replay ID for?
options: As a durable unique key to identify a specific event forever
To compute new Replay IDs by adding an offset, to jump anywhere in the stream
To guarantee ordering across every channel in the org
To resume a subscription from a known point after a disconnect, within the retention window
questions.explain: A Replay ID is a position marker for resuming a subscription. It isn't guaranteed unique across certain maintenance activities, and you should never compute new ones yourself — only reuse ones actually received.

questions.q: In a platform event trigger, what does throwing `EventBus.RetryableException` do?
options: It immediately rolls back the entire org transaction
It unsubscribes the trigger from future events permanently
It requests that the platform retry the entire trigger invocation for that batch of events
It converts the platform event into a custom object record
questions.explain: Throwing EventBus.RetryableException tells the platform to retry the whole trigger invocation for the current batch; EventBus.TriggerContext.retries tracks how many times that has already happened.

questions.q: Does Salesforce guarantee event ordering across two different channels, such as a platform event channel and a CDC change-event channel?
options: Yes, ordering is always preserved across every channel in the org
Only if both channels are high-volume
Only if Pub/Sub API is used instead of CometD
No — ordering is preserved within a single channel, but not guaranteed across different channels or event types
questions.explain: Delivery order is preserved per channel, but there is no platform-wide guarantee across different channels — cross-channel ordering requires an explicit sequencing field in the payload, not reliance on arrival order.
